title: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER
abstract: arXiv:2611.06988v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Forecasting foundation models are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for time series classification, but it remains unclear whether their pretrained representations offer an advantage over strong classifiers that do not require pretraining. This raises an important question: do these representations provide useful information beyond what the model architecture alone can capture, particularly when labelled data are scarce? We present a controlled benchmarking of two forecasting models, Reverso and Chronos-Bolt, on six large datasets from the MONSTER benchmark, using 1%, 10%, and 100% of the available training labels. We compare their frozen representations against four established time series classification methods and random-weight versions of the same forecasting models. translated_title: 大模型，小收益：MONSTER 基准上作为分类器的冻结预测模型
translated_abstract: 预测基础模型越来越多地被用作时间序列分类的冻结特征提取器，但它们的预训练表示是否比无需预训练的强分类器具有优势仍不清楚。这引出了一个重要问题：这些表示是否提供了模型架构本身所能捕获之外的有用信息，尤其是在标注数据稀缺的情况下？我们在 MONSTER 基准的六个大型数据集上，分别使用可用训练标签的 1%、10% 和 100%，对 Reverso 和 Chronos-Bolt 两个预测模型进行了受控基准测试。我们将它们的冻结表示与四种成熟的时间序列分类方法以及相同预测模型的随机权重版本进行比较。结果表明，在六个数据集中的五个上，预训练比随机权重的对应模型提升了分类准确率，收益最高达 23 个百分点……（原文截断）
tldr: 该论文在 MONSTER 基准上对冻结的预测基础模型（Reverso 和 Chronos-Bolt）表示进行受控评测，发现预训练相比随机权重模型仅带来小幅且不稳定的分类准确率提升，表明这些预训练表示未必优于无需预训练的强分类器，尤其在标注稀缺时其价值存疑。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a controlled benchmark on MONSTER showing that frozen pretrained forecasting representations (Reverso and Chronos-Bolt) yield only small and inconsistent classification gains over random-weight counterparts and established classifiers, questioning the added value of pretraining for time series classification.
